sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
Ink Drop's core gameplay mechanics are simple yet engaging. The objective of the game is to fill up a jar with ink drops. The game takes place on a single screen, with the jar located at the top and a stream of ink drops flowing from the bottom. The player must use their mouse, keyboard, or touch controls to guide the ink drops into the jar. Sounds easy, right? Well, it's not as simple as it sounds. The ink drops move at a steady pace, and the player must be quick on their toes to avoid obstacles. The obstacles come in the form of other objects on the screen, such as small balls, which can knock the ink drops off course. The player must navigate the ink drops through the obstacles to fill up the jar.

The game also features a life system, where the player starts with a set number of lives. Each time the player loses an ink drop, they lose a life. If the player loses all their lives, the game is over. However, the player can regain lost lives by watching ads. This adds a new layer of strategy to the game, as players must weigh the benefits of watching an ad against the risks of losing lives. The game also features a scoring system, where the player earns points for each ink drop they successfully guide into the jar. The score increases as the player progresses through the game, making it a fun and challenging experience.

The gameplay is smooth and fluid, with the ink drops moving at a steady pace. The controls are responsive, making it easy for players to navigate the ink drops through the obstacles. The game also features a variety of levels, each with its own unique obstacles and challenges. This adds a new layer of depth to the game, making it a fun and engaging experience for players of all ages.
